environment.description: Same EC2 instance and application code deployed behind an nginx reverse proxy (v1.24.0) running as a sidecar process on the same host. The nginx configuration includes a location block that appends response headers via add_header directive in the server context. The relevant header addition was part of a compliance remediation ticket (SECOPS-4471) that added several headers including one for script-src policy. The nginx conf.d/security-headers.conf file sets a restrictive policy that only permits script resources loaded from the application's own origin and a specific CDN hash, using nonce-less enforcement. Note: the application itself does NOT set this header - it is injected at the proxy layer, which means the Flask code has no awareness of it. The header uses 'strict-dynamic' is NOT present, and 'unsafe-inline' is explicitly absent from the script-src directive.

config.load_balancer: ALB with target group health checks
config.nginx_security_headers_conf: add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://cdn.enterprise.internal; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self';" always;
config.nginx_proxy_conf: proxy_hide_header Content-Security-Policy; (ensures app-level CSP if any is replaced)
config.additional_note: CSP report-uri not configured; violations are silent. Header applied via always flag ensuring it covers all response codes including 4xx/5xx.
